entities.summary: Mikołaj Trąba, of Trąby coat of arms, was a Polish Roman Catholic priest, Royal Notary from 1390, Deputy Chancellor of the Crown 1403–12, bishop of Halicz 1410–12, archbishop of Gniezno from 1412, and first primate of Poland 1417–22.

Mikołaj Trąba, a Polish Roman Catholic priest, played a pivotal role in shaping the political and ecclesiastical landscape of 15th-century Poland. Born in 1358 in Sandomierz, Trąba rose through the ranks to become the first primate of Poland, a position he held from 1417 to 1422. During his tenure, he oversaw the development of the Polish crown, established the bishopric of Halicz, and played a key role in the Polish-Lithuanian union. Trąba's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped shape the country's constitutional development and contributed to the growth of the Polish Reformation. His influence can be seen in the subsequent reforms of the Polish crown and the establishment of the Polish bishopric of Gniezno. Trąba's efforts also left a lasting impact on the Polish Catholic Church, as he worked to establish a stronger connection between the church and the crown. The Polish monarchs who succeeded Trąba, including Casimir IV Jagiellon and John I Albert, continued to build upon his foundations, solidifying Poland's position as a major power in Eastern Europe. Trąba's life and career serve as a testament to the enduring influence of the Polish crown and the power of the church in shaping the country's history.

Trąba was a key figure in the politics of the Polish-Lithuanian union, playing a significant role in the union's development and the establishment of the Polish crown. He was a close ally of Casimir IV Jagiellon, who would go on to become one of the most influential monarchs in Polish history. Trāba's relationship with Jagiellon was marked by mutual respect and trust, and the two men worked together to strengthen the union and promote the interests of the Polish crown. Trāba's involvement in the union also extended to his role as bishop of Halicz, where he worked to promote the interests of the Polish crown and to strengthen the connection between the church and the state.
